A.text: A solid sphere of radius r made of a soft material of bulk modulus K is surrounded by a liquid in a cylindrical container. A massless piston of cross section area 'a' floats on the surface of the liquid, covering entire cross-section of cylindrical container. When a mass m is placed on the surface of the piston to compress the liquid, the fractional decrement in the radius of the sphere, (dr/r), is
A.sol_text:
K = -V(dP/dV)

= (-dV/V) / (dP/K) = mg/(Ka)

⇒ (-3dr/r) = mg/(Ka)

⇒ dr/r = -mg/(3Ka)

A.subject: Physics
A.text: A source emits electromagnetic waves of wavelength 5 m, one beam reaches the observer directly and other after reflection from a water surface, travelling 2 m extra distance and with intensity reduced to 9/16 as compared to intensity due to the direct beam alone. The resultant intensity will be approximately (as compared to intensity due to direct beam alone)
A.sol_text:
Answer: (2)
Solution:
Path difference, Δx = 2 m
∴ Phase difference,
φ = 2π · (Δx/λ) = 2π · (2/5) = 144°
The reflected wave also suffers a phase reversal due to reflection
∴ Net phase difference = 36°
∴ Resultant intensity
= 1 + (9/16)I + 2 × √(1 · (9/16)I) cos 36°
= 2211/80 ≈ 44/16

A.subject: Physics
A.text: The greatest and shortest distance of a satellite from earth in an elliptical orbit is r₁ and r₂. Its distance from earth, when it is at perpendicular drawn to major axis from the earth, is
A.sol_text:
Answer: (2)
Hint:
Use equation of ellipse.
a = (r₁+r₂)/2

Solution:

Equation of ellipse:
(x²/a²) + (y²/b²) = 1

|x| = ae = a - r₂,

a = (r₁+r₂)/2

∴ (1 - e²/a²) × b²

⇒ y = 2r₁r₂/(r₁+r₂)

A.subject: Physics
A.text: If λ is the wavelength of first spectral line of Lyman series of a H-atom then what is the wavelength of first spectral line of Lyman series of a deuterium atom? [Given m_p is mass of proton and m_e is mass of electron]
A.sol_text:
Answer : (1)
Solution:
λ_d/λ_H = μ_H/μ_d
μ_H = reduced mass of Hydrogen
μ_d = reduced mass of deuterium
μ_H = (m_p m_e)/(m_p + m_e) = m_e(1 - m_e/m_p)
μ_d = (2m_p m_e)/(2m_p + m_e) = m_e[1 - m_e/(2m_p)]
λ_d/λ_H = [m_e(1 - m_e/m_p)]/[m_e(1 - m_e/(2m_p))]
= (1 - m_e/m_p)(1 + m_e/(2m_p))
λ_d = λ(1 - m_e/(2m_p))

A.text: A hoop and a disc of same mass and radius are made of a permanent magnetic material with their magnetic moment parallel to their respective axes. But the magnetic moment of hoop is twice of disc. They are placed in a uniform magnetic field in such a manner that their magnetic moments make a small angle with the field. A.sol_text:

A.text: Three resistors are connected in series across a 12 V battery. The first resistor has a value 1 Ω, second resistor has a voltage drop of 4 V and the third has a power dissipation of 12 W. Possible value of circuit current is
A.sol_text:

Solution:
Let the unknown resistors are R₂ and R₃.

I²R₃ = 12; IR₂ = 4

|4/R₂|²R₃ = 12; 16/R₂² × R₃ = 12; R₃ = (3/4)R₂²

I(1 + R₂ + R₃) = 12

⇒ (4/R₂)(1 + R₂ + (3/4)R₂²) = 12

⇒ 3R₂² - 8R₂ + 4 = 0 ⇒ R₂ = 2 Ω or (5/3)Ω

A.text: There is an ideal gas of molar mass M in a uniform gravitational acceleration g. The temperature of the gas varies with height h from earth as T = T₀[1 + ah] where a is a positive constant. The gas pressure P as a function of height h is given as (P₀ is pressure at surface of earth)
A.sol_text:
Use ideal gas equation and pressure variation with height
PV = nRT = nRT₀[1 + ah]

dp/dh = -ρg
⇒ dp = -ρgdh

P = (nM/ρ) = nRT₀[1 + ah]

⇒ ρ = (PM)/(RT₀[1+ah])

⇒ P = P₀/((1+ah)^(Mg/(aRT₀)))

B.text: In the figure shown a block of m is attached to a light spring of force constant K and an identical spring hangs from ceiling. Initially lower spring is in compressed state with compression equal to (3mg)/(k). When block is released it strikes upper spring and sticks to it. What is the amplitude of oscillation (in cm), after sticking? (Given mg = 20 N; K = 100√7 N/m.) (Natural length of springs are such that their end just touches each other.)
B.sol_text:
Velocity of block when it strikes upper spring V = √((k)/(m))√[((2mg)/(k))^2 - ((mg)/(k))^2] = √3√((k)/(m))((mg)/(k))

Where amplitude of oscillation for lower spring block is (2mg)/(k)

New equilibrium position is at x = (mg)/(2k) from relaxed state of upper spring.

If new amplitude is A' then

v = √((2k)/(m))√[A'^2 - ((mg)/(2k))^2] = √3√((k)/(m))((mg)/(k))

Or, A' = (√7)/(2)(mg)/(k)
B.nvt_note: Give your answer as the nearest integer.

B.subject: Physics
B.text: Two runners Ram and Shyam in a 144 m race start from the same place, but one runner gives the other a time advantage. The first runner, Ram, starts right away and runs at a constant velocity of 8.0 m/s. The second runner Shyam, waits for two seconds and then runs at a velocity of 9.0 m/s. B.sol_text:
Time taken by Ram and finish the race
t₁ = 144/8 = 18 sec

Time taken by Shyam to finish the race
t₂ = 144/9 = 16 sec

So, they finish the race simultaneously together
Hence, their separation is zero.

A.subject: Chemistry
A.text: A good secondary cell can undergo a large number of discharging and charging cycles. The most important secondary cell is lead storage battery, commonly used in automobiles and inverters. Which of the following reactions occur at anode during charging of lead storage battery?
A.sol_text:
Answer: (4)
Solution:
The cell reaction where battery is in use are given below:
Anode: Pb(s) + SO₄²⁻(aq) → PbSO₄(s) + 2e⁻
Cathode: PbO₂(s) + SO₄²⁻(aq) + 4H⁺(aq.) + 2e⁻ → PbSO₄(s) + 2H₂O(l)
Overall reaction →
Pb(s) + PbO₂(s) + 2H₂SO₄(aq) → 2PbSO₄(s) + 2H₂O(l)
On charging the battery the reaction is reversed and PbSO₄(s) on anode and cathode is converted into Pb and PbO₂, respectively.

The spin only magnetic moment for [Cu(NH₃)₄]²⁺ ion is _____ × 10⁻¹ BM

Solution:

Cu - atom (Z = 29): 3d: ↑↓ ↑↓ ↑↓ ↑↓ ↑, 4s: ↑, 4p: (empty)

With dsp² hybridisation, with one unpaired e⁻

∴ spin only magnetic moment = μ = √(n(n+2))

μ = √(1(1+2)) = √3 = 1.73

μ = 1.73 BM

μ = 17.3 × 10⁻¹ BM

μ ≈ 17 × 10⁻¹ BM

Answer: 17

A.text: Let A = [a_ij]₃×₃ be a matrix where a_ij ∈ {0, 1} ∀ 1 ≤ i, j ≤ 3. If s_i = Σ_{k=1}^{3} a_ik and t_j = Σ_{k=1}^{3} a_kj, then the probability that the product (s₁·s₂·s₃·t₁·t₂·t₃) is an odd integer, is

log₁₀ x = 1
